correctness.summary: The lower bound follows from shortest directed paths and the exact Padé coefficients a1,...,a7: positive through a5, a6=0, a7<0. The only seven-state exceptional distance-six case has (Q^7)_ij<0, so its leading Padé contribution is positive. The eight-state pure-birth witness is evaluated by Jordan functional calculus; the first-to-absorbing entry has a strictly increasing polynomial sign factor with one positive root, while the nearest-neighbor entry changes sign at 2sqrt(3). All remaining entries are nonnegative between those endpoints. Symbolic verification reproduces the identities and row sums.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2012 Zappavigna-Colaneri-Kirkland-Shorten paper already proves arbitrarily-small [2/2] Padé positivity failure for an 8x8 nonnegative nilpotent shift and for a related Hurwitz Metzler shift; absolute-monotonicity theory also gives zero uniform radius for the fourth-order (2,2) rational class. The present claim is narrower and sharper under the conservative CTMC constraint: minimal state dimension eight plus the exact stochasticity window of an eight-state pure-birth generator. Searches of synonymous Markov/Padé/Gauss-Legendre formulations and current related work did not locate this classification. A recent 2026 Fokker-Planck rational-map preprint was only available at abstract level, leaving residual risk.

value.summary: The result gives a sharp finite-state failure certificate for a fourth-order A-stable Padé/Gauss-Legendre end-step map used as an approximate Markov transition operator. It shows conservation does not prevent arbitrarily-small positivity loss, proves this cannot happen below eight states, and exhibits a nonmonotone step-size window where stochasticity is restored.

limitations: Exact arithmetic and finite real CTMC generators only.
The result concerns end-step entrywise positivity, not internal Runge-Kutta stages.
The seven-state guarantee is local for each fixed generator and is not uniform over unbounded rates.
The exact global positivity window is for one eight-state pure-birth generator.
No analogous classification is claimed for other Padé orders or Runge-Kutta methods.
No floating-point, nonlinear, efficiency, or error-versus-cost claim is made.
Full theorem-level comparison with Itkin-Kazbek (2026) and end-to-end inspection of van de Griend-Kraaijevanger (1986) remain residual originality risks.
Independent audit has not been performed.
